1JOHN POE, Minister for the Interior, by virtue of the powers
conferred by Section 12(1) of the Corrective

    Improvements:—Section 57 of the Land Act 1962-74 provides that
an Agricultural Lease shall contain conditions prescribing
the minimum improvements to be carried out by the lessee. Conditions
applicable to the lease above are as follows:

       (a) Of the land suitable for cultivation the following

proportions shall be planted in a good and husbandlike manner with
           a crop or pasture species of economic value which shall
be harvested regularly in accordance with sound commercial
           practice-

            One-fifth in the first period of 5 years of the term;
            Three-fifths in the first period of 10 years of the
term;
            Four-fifths in the first period of 15 years of the term;

           and during the remainder of the term four-fifths of the
land so suitable shall be kept so planted.

       (b) That portion of the lease to be utilised for grazing
shall be stocked with a minimum of 1 head of great cattle per 5
           hectares within 3 years from the date of grant and shall
be kept so stocked to that minimum for the remainder of the
           term.
       (c) That portion of the lease which shall be utilised for
grazing shall, from within 2 years of the date of grant, be fenced
           externally except in such parts where the natural
features make this unnecessary, with a barbed-wire fence of not less
           than 4 strands, the topmost of which shall be not less
than 1 metre above the ground and having posts not more
           than 4.5 metres apart and strainer posts at least every
100 metres, the said fence to be kept well-strained and in a stock-
           proof condition.
       (d) The area which is to be utilised for grazing shall within
3 years from the date of grant be subdivided by fences into a
           minimum of 4 paddocks none of which shall enclose more
than half of the total area to be used for grazing, and for
           the duration of the lease the said area shall be kept so
subdivided and the said fence maintained in stock-proof con-
           dition.

       (e) Yards and handling facilities to the satisfaction of the
Land Board shall be constructed within 2 years from the date of
           grant.
       (f) Provided always that if at the end of the first 2 years
of the lease it appears that reasonable efforts are not being made
           to fulfil the improvement conditions, the Minister for
Lands may, by notice in the Gazette, and in accordance with
           the provisions of the Land Act 1962-74, forfeit the
lease.

   Residence Condition:—The lessee or his agent shall take up
residency or occupancy of his block within 6 months from the
date of grant.

each lease required. Applications not conforming to these

requirements will be rejected as informal.

starch-reduced bread, protein-increased bread or

         milk bread as defined in this Order or fancy bread;


     "milk bread" means bread which is made into loaves and which
contains no less than four parts per centurn

         by weight of non-fat milk solids calculated on the water-
free substance;


     "starch-reduced bread" or "protein increased bread" means bread
which is made into loaves and which

         contains not less than two and seven-tenths part per centum
by weight of nitrogen calculated on the

         water-free substance;


     "unwrapped" in relation to the sale of any bread means that
such bread is not wrapped as defined in

         this Order.


     "wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread that such
bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery to

the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in waxed or
grease-proof paper, cellulose film, poly-

         thene or other similar wrapping and that such bread was so
enclosed when sold;


     "foil-wrapped" means in relation to the sale of any bread that
such bread is fully enclosed prior to delivery

         to the place at which the bread is sold by retail, in
aluminium or other foil, and that such bread was

            so enclosed when sold.
